title: Natural history of thyroid function in ageing: an individual participant data analysis of 137 488 participants from 31 prospective cohort studies
authors: Xu Y, Hysaj O, Qi X, Feller M, Pingitore A, Brown SJ, et al.
population: 31 population-based cohorts in Europe, the USA, Asia, Brazil and Australia; median age 60 years (range 18 to 106); participants with thyroid disease or thyroid-altering medication at baseline or during follow-up excluded
funder: There was no funding source for this study.
authorConflicts: Several authors reported grants or fees from companies, including personal fees from Merck KGaA and Berlin Chemie for one author and consulting fees from IBSA and others for another.
result: Cross-sectionally, older age was associated with higher TSH in iodine-sufficient regions and lower TSH in iodine-insufficient regions; longitudinally TSH rose with age regardless of iodine status. From age 18 to 100 years TSH rose by 0.61 mIU/l in women and 0.99 mIU/l in men from iodine-sufficient regions, with greater variability from age 65. Against stable thyroid function, rising TSH with stable or falling free T4 carried a mortality hazard ratio of 1.80 (95% CI 1.57 to 2.06), and falling TSH with stable or rising free T4 1.94 (1.68 to 2.24).
